The values present on a grain column

Source: R/inventory.R
grain_values.Rd

Answers "which channels are in this plan?" — for whatever the user called their channel column. The package never privileges a column name: channel is simply a dimension someone chose to key on, and a plan may key on media_type or vehicle instead. So this takes the column by name and errors, listing the alternatives, when asked for one the plan does not have.

Usage

grain_values(plan, col = NULL)

Arguments

plan

A MediaPlan.

col

Name of a single grain column. NULL (the default) returns a named list covering every grain column, including the week.

Value

Sorted unique values for col, in the column's own type; or a named list of those vectors when col is NULL.

Details

The values are exactly what build_scenario()'s target accepts, so an answer from here can be passed straight into an edit without translation.

Examples

p <- media_plan_from_df(
  data.frame(channel = c("TV", "TV", "Search"),
             partner = c("NBC", "ESPN", "Google"),
             planned_spend = c(30, 20, 50)),
  grain = c("channel", "partner"), name = "Q3 plan"
)

grain_values(p, "channel")
#> [1] "Search" "TV"    
grain_values(p)
#> $channel
#> [1] "Search" "TV"    
#> 
#> $partner
#> [1] "ESPN"   "Google" "NBC"   
#>
